# Results — Study 807 (Salience-Theory Returns)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Cosemans &
Frehen (2021), applying Bordalo-Gennaioli-Shleifer salience: a name whose **salient days were
UP** relative to the market (a high salience-theory value ST) is over-priced and earns **lower**
future returns, so a long-low-ST / short-high-ST book should earn a positive spread. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
Reported as-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is
dropped). Fingerprint `357fd262912f` (panel Close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Signal | each name's **trailing-21-day salience-theory value** ST: for each day `σ = \|rᵢ−rₘ\| / (\|rᵢ\|+\|rₘ\|+θ)`, θ=0.1 (market = equal-weight cross-section mean); rank the window's days by salience and give declining decision weights `δ^rank` (δ=0.7, rank 0 = most salient), normalised; ST = salience-weighted mean of `rᵢ−rₘ`. Known at the close of `t−1` (one `shift`) |
| Sort | each day rank the cross-section by the signal; **long the bottom 30%** (low ST), **short the top 30%** (high ST), equal-weight; measure the day-`t` forward return of each book |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t−1` → hold day `t`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per day on the long-short book; the short book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the daily spread; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled low-vs-high books; a 1,000-permutation placebo; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership** list of names
that are liquid mega-caps *today*, so the magnitudes are an **upper bound**. Crucially, the
salience-theory premium is documented on the **broad** cross-section (small, illiquid, lottery-like
names included); a 50-mega-cap survivor panel is exactly where it is *least* likely to appear —
which is what we find.

## The headline — long-low-ST / short-high-ST spread

Daily equal-weight bottom-30% (low ST) minus top-30% (high ST) spread (n = **4,125** days):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **spread (long low-ST − short high-ST)** | **−1.00 bps/day** |
| Newey-West(10) *t* | **−0.78** |
| one-sample *t* | −0.74 |
| low-ST book / high-ST book | +7.49 bps / +8.49 bps (Welch *t* = −0.37) |
| gross spread Sharpe (no cost) | −0.18 |

The claimed edge **does not replicate.** Cosemans & Frehen predict a *positive* long-low/short-high
spread (low-ST names out-earn); on this mega-cap universe the spread is **−1.00 bps/day with
NW *t* = −0.78** — statistically indistinguishable from zero, and if anything *very weakly* the
wrong sign. The two books earn essentially the same forward return (+7.49 vs +8.49 bps, Welch
*t* = −0.37). There is simply no salience premium here.

## Placebo — is the (tiny) spread a lucky alignment of the sort?

Keep the trailing-ST sort but read each day's forward returns from a **column-permuted** panel
(signal → outcome link broken), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **−1.00 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | +0.009 bps (0.896) |
| position of observed | ≈ **1.1σ into the left tail** (right-tail p = 0.867) |

The permutation null centres at zero; the observed −1.00 bps sits barely ~1.1σ away — right in
the noise. Nothing to explain: there is no reliable relation, in either direction.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=1,991) | −0.80 bps | **−0.60** |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=2,134) | −1.19 bps | **−0.55** |

Flat and insignificant in both halves — not one era masking another.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per day on the long-short book; short pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/day | cost/day | net/day | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | −1.00 bps | 2.14 bps | **−3.14 bps** | −2.32 | −0.57 | −7.9%/yr |
| **5 bps** | −1.00 bps | 10.14 bps | **−11.14 bps** | −8.23 | −2.03 | −28.1%/yr |

With no gross edge to begin with, any friction just deepens the loss. Even the *sign-flipped* book
(long high-ST) would earn only +1.00 bps/day gross — less than half the 2.14 bps/day round-trip at
a mere 1 bp one-way. **Mirage** in either direction.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel with a persistent latent "salient-upside tilt" that makes a name's salient
days up-days (high ST) and (with `edge>0`) depresses its forward mean. No network.

| world | spread NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.26** (sd 0.91), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** |
| planted (`edge = 0.0016`, seed 807) | **+4.31** (Welch *t* = +4.46) |

The detector recovers a *planted* salience relation cleanly and fires on only 1/20 nulls (~the
nominal 5% rate) — so the flat real-tape result is a genuine null, not a broken detector. *(A
faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The Cosemans-Frehen salience-theory premium does **not** show up on 50 liquid
  US mega-caps. The specified long-low-ST / short-high-ST spread is **−1.00 bps/day** (NW
  *t* = **−0.78**) — indistinguishable from zero, flat in both eras (*t* = −0.60 / −0.55), ~1.1σ from
  the centre of a 1,000-permutation placebo, with a clean 20-seed synthetic control. The claimed edge
  is absent (it is a broad-cross-section, small-cap-inclusive phenomenon); mega-caps are where it
  should not appear.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no gross edge to harvest; the specified book loses net (−3.14
  bps/day at 1 bp, −11.14 at 5 bps), and even the data-mined sign-flip is eaten by the round-trip
  friction at 1 bp.
